title: Seven Reasons Carrots and Sticks (Often) Don’t Work . . .
coreMove: Conditional rewards are risky when the work needs insight, persistence, or ethics, because control can crowd out the motive you wanted.

exampleSpecs.audience: Claudia, a museum educator deciding whether to prize every answer
exampleSpecs.stakes: A children's desk needs energy without turning curiosity into a contest.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the reward crowding out the museum's learning motive.

exampleSpecs.audience: Niko, a design lead protecting exploratory work
exampleSpecs.stakes: A sprint team wants speed, but the problem needs a wider search.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the candle-problem warning in a design sprint.

exampleSpecs.audience: Yara, a preschool director reading a fee as a social signal
exampleSpecs.stakes: A pickup policy could turn responsibility into a purchasable delay.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a social norm becoming a market bargain.

exampleSpecs.audience: Hassan, a sales leader deciding whether a target invites gaming
exampleSpecs.stakes: A compensation review has to distinguish healthy direction from a narrow scoreboard.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a reward that improves numbers while corrupting judgment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Marta, a volunteer coordinator preserving choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: A community table needs commitments without making service feel bought.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how autonomy protects volunteer motive.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ellis, a security lead designing a bug bounty carefully
exampleSpecs.stakes: A bounty should find flaws without training people to chase payout at any cost.
